skill.name: Specialist and technical words in context
skill.why: Each subject has exact words. Use them so readers know exactly what you mean.
skill.how: Use nearby clues to work out a technical word. Write with the word an expert uses.

steps.say: Don't know a science word? Check the words around it.

show.nudge: That's what changed. Which part tells you what happened to its water?
That's the hard word. Which words tell you what it means?
That says when. Read the next sentence for the meaning.

show.text: Its water turned from a liquid into a gas.

steps.ask: Tap the clue that tells you what evaporated means.
steps.win: Yes! Evaporate means turning from liquid to gas.

steps.say: Animal experts have exact words too.

options.text: an animal that sleeps in trees
options.reason: Koalas do sleep in trees, but what does the next sentence say?
Check the clue. What do koalas eat?

steps.win: Yes! 'Eat only plants' told you. Herbivore is the expert word.

steps.say: Careful! Some everyday words mean something new in science.

show.text: Your body is made of millions of tiny

options.text: a tiny building block of living things
a small room in a jail
options.reason: That is the everyday meaning. Is your body made of jail rooms?
Blood is only one part of you. The clue says your whole body is made of them.

steps.win: Yes! In science, a cell is a living building block.

steps.say: In a report, use the exact word.
show: The ice ___ in the sun and made a puddle.
steps.ask: Which science word fits the gap?

options.reason: Evaporate means a liquid turning into a gas. Is ice a liquid?
Froze means a liquid turning solid. The ice was already frozen.

steps.win: Yes! Melted: a solid turning into a liquid.

steps.say: Music has specialist words too. The clue is close by.

options.reason: Check the clue: sped up, danced faster. Is that about loudness?
You can't speed up a name. What got faster?

steps.win: Yes! Tempo means speed. Specialist words are also called technical words.

terms.means: An exact word for one subject, like evaporate or tempo. Also called a technical word.
Nearby words that tell you what the specialist word means.

card.test: Use the clues around the word. In a subject, an everyday word can mean something new.

weDo.text: When water vapour cools, it ___ into tiny drops on the cold window.
weDo.hint: A gas is turning into drops of liquid. Which word means that?
weDo.success: Condenses. When a gas cools and turns into a liquid, it condenses.

options.reason: Evaporates is the opposite: a liquid turning into a gas. Here a gas turns into drops.
Melts means a solid turning into a liquid, like ice. Water vapour is a gas.

weDo.text: Tully took a mark right in front of goal.
weDo.prompt: In footy, what does 'mark' mean here?
weDo.hint: Think about what a player does with the ball.
weDo.success: A clean catch from a kick. In footy, catching a long kick cleanly is called taking a mark.

options.text: a clean catch from a kick

options.reason: That's the everyday meaning. 'Took a mark in front of goal' tells you it's part of the game.
That's a school meaning. You can't take a score out of ten in front of goal.

creature.name: Termolin
creature.blurb: A platypus whose bill buzzes when it senses a specialist word. It can tell a footy mark from a mark on your homework.

write.ask: Rewrite this sentence for a science report. Swap the everyday words for one specialist word.
given: On the hot day, the water in the puddle turned into a gas.
checks: I used the word a science expert would use
My sentence still means the same thing
write.model: On the hot day, the water in the puddle evaporated.

encounters.frame: Tully is calling the game on footy radio.
encounters.text: Tully kicked the ball between the two tall posts. That scored a ___.
encounters.prompt: Which footy word fits?
encounters.success: Goal. In footy, kicking the ball between the two tall posts scores a goal, worth six points.

options.reason: A behind goes between a tall post and a short post. This kick went between the two tall ones.
A try is a rugby word for putting the ball down over the line. Tully kicked it through the posts.

encounters.frame: The Termolin's bill is buzzing at Zed's space poster.
encounters.prompt: Tap the space word that names Earth's path around the Sun.
encounters.success: Orbit. An orbit is the curved path one object takes around another in space.

parts.reason: Travels is an everyday word for moving. Which word names the path?
Year tells you how long the trip takes, not what the path is called.

encounters.frame: The Termolin found a pile of sentences after band practice and sport training.
encounters.prompt: Use the clues in each sentence. Match each word to the right bag.
encounters.success: The clues tell you. Ruck, handball and boundary are sport words. Tempo, chorus and rhythm are music words.

items.text: 'ruck' in: The ruck jumped high to tap the ball.
items.reason: Jumping to tap the ball tells you the ruck is a footy player.

items.text: 'handball' in: Jai punched the footy to Tully in a handball.
items.reason: Punching the footy to a teammate is a kind of pass in footy.

items.text: 'boundary' in: The batter hit the ball over the boundary.
items.reason: A batter hitting the ball tells you this is cricket, a sport.

items.text: 'tempo' in: The band slowed the tempo for the sad song.
items.reason: Slowing it for a song tells you tempo is how fast music goes.

items.text: 'chorus' in: Everyone sang the chorus again at the end.
items.reason: Singing it again tells you the chorus is the part of a song that repeats.

items.text: 'rhythm' in: Mo clapped the rhythm of the drum beat.
items.reason: Clapping a drum beat tells you rhythm is the pattern of beats in music.

encounters.frame: Gus wants to see the tiny germs in his slime. He checks his science book first.
encounters.prompt: Build the sentence with the right tool for seeing tiny things.
encounters.success: Microscope. A microscope makes tiny things look much bigger.

accept: Gus looked at the slime under a microscope.
body.reason: Germs are tiny, not far away. Check what the science book says each tool does.

encounters.text: A telescope makes faraway things look closer. A microscope makes tiny things look bigger.

encounters.frame: Indi's art diary has the wrong art word.
encounters.prompt: Tap the wrong art word, then choose the right one.
encounters.success: Palette. A palette is the board artists mix their paints on.

parts.reason: Mixed is right. Blue and yellow mixed together make green.
Canvas is right. It's the cloth artists paint their picture on.

options.reason: A frame goes around a finished picture. You don't mix paint on it.
An apron keeps paint off your clothes. You don't mix paint on it.

encounters.frame: Wren is reading the dive school's safety rules.
encounters.text: The diver checked the current before she jumped in.
encounters.prompt: What does 'current' mean here?
encounters.success: The way the water is flowing. Divers check the current so it doesn't sweep them away.

options.text: the way the water is flowing

options.reason: That's the everyday meaning, as in 'current news'. A diver about to jump in checks the water.
That's what current means for electricity. The diver is about to jump into water, not touch a wire.

encounters.frame: Gus is writing up his worst experiment yet.
encounters.text: Gus left some bread in a jar for two weeks. Fuzzy green ___ grew all over it.
encounters.prompt: Which science word fits?
encounters.success: Mould. Mould is a fungus that grows as fuzzy patches on old food.

options.reason: Moss is a small green plant that grows on rocks and trees, not on old bread.
Algae grows in water, like the green slime in a fish tank. This bread was in a dry jar.

encounters.frame: Zed is reading the program for the school concert.
encounters.prompt: Tap the specialist music word that means 'getting louder bit by bit'.
encounters.success: Crescendo. A crescendo is a part of the music that grows gradually louder.

parts.reason: Band is an everyday word for a group of musicians.
Windows is an everyday word. It shows how loud the music got, but it isn't a music word.

encounters.frame: Gus's science folder fell open. Help the Termolin sort the pages.
encounters.prompt: Use the clues in each sentence. Match each word to the right page.
encounters.success: Orbit, comet and galaxy are space words. Skeleton, lungs and artery are words about the human body.

items.text: 'orbit' in: The Moon travels in an orbit around Earth.
items.reason: Travelling around Earth tells you an orbit is a path through space.

items.text: 'comet' in: A comet streaked past with a long, icy tail.
items.reason: Streaking past with an icy tail tells you a comet travels through space.

items.text: 'galaxy' in: Our Sun is one of billions of stars in the galaxy.
items.reason: Billions of stars tells you a galaxy is a huge group of stars in space.

items.text: 'skeleton' in: Your skeleton holds your body up like a frame of bones.
items.reason: A frame of bones tells you the skeleton is part of your body.

items.text: 'lungs' in: Your lungs fill with air when you breathe in.
items.reason: Filling with air when you breathe tells you lungs are part of your body.

items.text: 'artery' in: The artery carried blood away from the heart.
items.reason: Carrying blood from the heart tells you an artery is part of your body.

encounters.frame: Gus's robot repair notes name the wrong part.
encounters.prompt: Tap the wrong word, then choose the right technical word.
encounters.success: Sensor. A sensor is the part of a robot that detects things around it, like walls.

parts: Gus's robot keeps crashing. It can't

parts.reason: See is the clue. The broken part must be the one that detects things.

parts: is broken. Gus will fix it

parts.reason: Tonight is fine. It just says when Gus will do the repair.

options.reason: A flat battery would stop the robot moving at all. It couldn't keep crashing.
Wheels help a robot move. A broken wheel can't stop it seeing the wall.

encounters.frame: Wren's rock pool guide says: when the tide goes out, the rock pools appear.
encounters.prompt: Build the sentence that matches Wren's guide.
encounters.success: At low tide. When the tide goes out, the water is low and the rock pools are uncovered.

accept: At low tide, the rock pools are easy to explore.
body.reason: At high tide the sea covers the rock pools. You can only explore them when the tide is low.

encounters.frame: Mo is following a recipe for once.
encounters.text: Mo has to ___ the cream: beat it fast until it's thick and fluffy.
encounters.prompt: Which cooking word fits?
encounters.success: Whip. To whip cream is to beat it fast until it's thick and fluffy.

options.reason: Simmer means cook gently on a low heat. The recipe says to beat the cream fast.
Knead means press and fold dough with your hands. You can't knead cream.

encounters.frame: Wren is reading a sign at the wildlife park's bat house.
encounters.text: Flying foxes are nocturnal. They sleep upside down through the day and fly out to feed after dark.
encounters.prompt: What does 'nocturnal' mean here?
encounters.success: Active at night. Sleeping through the day and feeding after dark is exactly what nocturnal animals do.

options.reason: Flying foxes can fly, but the clues are about sleeping by day and feeding after dark. Nocturnal is about time.
They do sleep upside down, but the clues point to when they're awake. Nocturnal is about time.
The sign doesn't say what they eat. The clues are about day and dark, so nocturnal is about time.

encounters.frame: The Termolin's bill is buzzing at one word in Tully's match report.
encounters.prompt: Tap the word that has a special footy meaning here, different from its everyday meaning.
encounters.success: Mark. In footy, the mark is the spot where a player caught the ball. An opponent stands on it.

parts.reason: Stood means the same in footy as anywhere else.
Kick means the same in footy as it does in the backyard.
Metres is a measuring word. It means the same everywhere.

encounters.frame: Wren's nature notes say: a predator hunts other animals. Its prey is the animal it hunts.
encounters.prompt: Build the sentence that matches Wren's notes.
encounters.success: The fox hunts the rabbit, so the fox is the predator and the rabbit is its prey.

accept: The fox is a predator, and the rabbit is its prey.
body.reason: Foxes hunt rabbits. The hunter is the predator, and the animal it hunts is its prey.

encounters.frame: Indi is writing up the school concert for the newsletter. The Termolin spots one music word used wrongly.
encounters.prompt: Tap the music word that's wrong, then choose the right one.
encounters.success: Tempo. The drummer sets the speed of the music. Change the speed and nobody can dance in time.

parts.reason: The chorus is the part of a song that repeats. Choirs do sing it.
Harmony means different notes that sound good together. That fits a choir.

parts: . But the drummer kept changing the

parts.reason: Dance is fine. It's a clue to which word is wrong.

options.reason: Changing key changes which notes the tune uses, not its speed. The clue is about keeping time.
The melody is the tune, and drums don't play the tune. The clue is about keeping time.
The choir sings the chorus, not the drummer. The clue is about keeping time.

encounters.frame: Indi's poster for the reef centre has one wrong word.
encounters.prompt: Tap the word that makes the fact wrong, then choose the right one.
encounters.success: Lack. Invertebrates have no backbone, which is how an octopus squeezes through tiny gaps.

parts.reason: Octopuses is fine. The poster is about them.
Invertebrates is the right word. The mistake is in what the poster says it means.
Squeeze is the clue. Only an animal with no bones could squeeze through tiny gaps.

options.reason: Invertebrates have no backbone at all, so they can't need one.
Invertebrates have no backbone, so there's nothing to use.
Invertebrates have no backbone, so there's nothing to break. And breaking one wouldn't help you squeeze.

encounters.frame: Zed is complaining about his game in the class group chat.
encounters.text: My game lags when too many players join. The characters freeze for a second, then jump forward.
encounters.prompt: What does 'lags' mean in gaming?
encounters.success: Runs slowly and falls behind. The game can't keep up, so the characters freeze and then jump ahead.

options.reason: A crash would close the game. Here the characters freeze for a second and then keep going.

options.text: has a mistake in its code
options.reason: That's a bug. The clue is that it only happens when too many players join.
The characters freeze, which is the opposite of running faster.

encounters.frame: Gus is writing up his volcano experiment. He has four drafts of the key sentence.
encounters.text: Gus mixed vinegar and bicarb soda. Foam gushed out of the bottle, and a new gas was made.
encounters.prompt: Which sentence would a scientist write in the report?
encounters.success: A chemical reaction makes something new, like this gas. The specialist word tells the reader exactly what happened.

options.text: The vinegar and bicarb soda made a mixture that went totally crazy.
options.reason: A mixture makes nothing new, but a new gas was made. And 'went crazy' is vague.

options.text: The vinegar and bicarb soda formed a solution that fizzed a lot.
options.reason: A solution is one thing dissolved in another. Nothing new is made in a solution.

options.text: The vinegar and bicarb soda did a cool science thing that made foam.
options.reason: A cool science thing is vague. A scientist names exactly what happened.

options.text: The vinegar and bicarb soda had a chemical reaction that made a new gas.

encounters.frame: The art show program describes Indi's landscape.
encounters.prompt: Tap the word that has a special art meaning here, different from its everyday meaning.
encounters.success: Perspective. Usually it means a point of view. In art, it's drawing far-away things smaller to show depth.

parts.reason: Used means the same in art as anywhere else.
Road is an everyday word. It's what Indi painted, not an art term.
Shrink means getting smaller, in art or anywhere else. Which word here is an art term?

parts: towards the horizon, giving her flat painting real depth.

encounters.frame: Gus's space dictionary says: a meteor is a space rock burning up in our sky. A meteorite is one that survives and lands on the ground.
encounters.prompt: Build the sentence that matches Gus's space dictionary.
encounters.success: Meteorite. The rock reached the ground, and a space rock that lands is a meteorite.

accept: The farmer found a meteorite in her paddock the morning after the meteor shower.
body.reason: A meteor burns up in the sky, so nobody can find one in a paddock. Landed space rocks are meteorites.

encounters.frame: The word 'pitch' turns up all over the island. The Termolin needs each one sorted.
encounters.prompt: Match each sentence to the meaning 'pitch' has in it.
encounters.success: Clues tell you which pitch: a playing field, how high a sound is, or a talk to win people over.

bins: how high or low a sound is
a short talk to sell an idea

items.text: The groundskeeper rolled the cricket pitch until it was flat and hard.
items.reason: Rolled flat and hard tells you this pitch is the ground the game is played on.

items.text: Heavy rain flooded the pitch before the match could start.
items.reason: A flooded pitch stops a match, so this is the playing field.

items.text: The soprano held a note at an astonishingly high pitch.
items.reason: A high note tells you this pitch is about sound.

items.text: The violinist tightened her string until the pitch was perfect.
items.reason: Tightening a string changes how high it sounds, so this pitch is about sound.

items.text: Halfway through his solo, Mo's voice cracked and jumped to a squeaky pitch.
items.reason: A squeaky voice is about how high a sound is, so this pitch is about sound.

items.text: Zed's two-minute pitch convinced the judges to fund his game.
items.reason: Convincing judges to fund something means this pitch was a talk to sell an idea.

items.text: The inventor practised her pitch before meeting the investors.
items.reason: Investors decide whether to back an idea, so this pitch is a sales talk.

encounters.frame: Gus's coding notes for the robot dance-off have the wrong technical word.
encounters.prompt: Tap the wrong word, then choose the right technical word.
encounters.success: Loop. In coding, a loop is a set of instructions that repeats, which is why the move happened ten times.

parts.reason: Repeated is the clue. Something in the code made the move happen again and again.
Dance is fine. It's the move the robot was doing.
Ten is fine. It tells you how many times the move repeated.

parts: times, because Gus had put the instruction inside a

options.reason: A variable stores a value, like a score. It doesn't make instructions repeat.
A sensor detects things around the robot. You can't put an instruction inside one.
A password keeps something locked. It doesn't make instructions repeat.

encounters.frame: Maxx Vantablack is live, holding up a cage. Wren knows he's got his science word wrong.
encounters.text: 'This creature is extinct!' Maxx shouted at the camera. 'There are only three of them left in the whole world, and I've got one.'
encounters.prompt: Which science word means what Maxx was trying to say?
encounters.success: Endangered means only a few are left and it could die out. Extinct means none are left at all.

options.reason: Nocturnal means active at night. Maxx is talking about how few are left.
An invasive species spreads into places it doesn't belong. Maxx says there are only three left.
Fossilised means turned to stone over millions of years. Maxx's creature is alive in a cage.
